verdict: Lend selectively to Chennai auto-component makers with export or non-ICE diversification; avoid single-OEM, ICE-concentrated and ride-hailing-dependent auto borrowers — OK at portfolio level, but Tamil Nadu's GST stress means structure each deal tightly.
title: Chennai Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative: **Pricing power sits with whoever holds design complexity** — ICRA notes diesel fuel-injection makers enjoy strong pricing power from design complexity, while engine-part suppliers face higher obsolescence risk as EVs spread [11]. So when a proposal lands, check the product's design content and the OEM's dependence on it; if the part is a commodity bracket, ask what stops the OEM from re-sourcing.

## What has changed now
**National output is running hot: IIP NIC 29 is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D].** Chennai peers confirm it — Wheels India's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 36% to Rs 1,598 crore and net profit nearly doubled to Rs 53 crore, with exports up 30% to Rs 388 crore and US sales up about 50% [1]; Motherson Sumi Wiring profit rose 35% to Rs 223 crore on revenue up 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore [4]. **But bank credit is growing +27.0% against output of +19.2%, a +7.8 pp gap [D]** — part of the lending is funding working capital stretch, not just volume. And **Tamil Nadu GST is -3.2% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, 9.3 pp slower [D]** — a genuine local stress signal. Note the local press here is thin on components; the auto-driver stories [2][3] are about ride-hailing, not manufacturing, so lean on first principles and peers.

## Where to grow
**Pursue exporters and diversifiers.** Wheels India's US construction-equipment and data-centre demand [1] and ASK Automotive's EV component order wins and export push [5] show where the growth is. Target Chennai tier-2 suppliers with (a) export or non-ICE revenue, (b) more than one OEM customer, (c) EV-agnostic product design. **Avoid single-OEM, ICE-engine-part-concentrated units and anything tied to ride-hailing auto loans** — Chennai drivers report trips halved and fares unchanged since 2013 [2].

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the P&L.** Rating work shows gross current assets averaging 160-170 days [10] and flags Debt/EBITDA above 2.5-2.75x as a red line [10]. So set the drawing power on a 160-170 day cycle, cap Debt/EBITDA at 2.5x as a covenant, and take monthly stock-and-debtor statements, monthly GST returns, and quarterly hedging confirmations — ICRA's analytical focus is on hedging policy and exposure relative to profits [8].

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the gap between credit growth and output [D] and the state GST trend [D].** If a borrower's GST turnover falls two quarters running while its bank debt rises, cut limits. If Debt/EBITDA crosses 2.5x [10], stop fresh disbursal.
